svg.title: Update and remove installed packages.
svg.desc: Refreshing package information is different from upgrading installed packages. Debian/Ubuntu apt update then apt upgrade and Fedora dnf upgrade --refresh update installed software using configured repositories. A labelled before and after depicts an illustrative old package version becoming a newer version. Separate distro-labelled remove commands use nano as an example, with a nearby warning about proposed removals and dependencies. Removing an editor normally leaves personal text files but does not create a backup. Administrative permission and repository access are prerequisites.
svg.text: Refresh = read available versions. Upgrade = update software already installed.
Needs admin permission and repository access. Review proposed changes before confirming.
After confirmation: installed packages get available upgrades. Illustrative versions:
Remove an installed package: nano is the example editor.
WARNING: review upgrades and removals before confirming, including related packages.
Removing an editor normally keeps your text files. Package removal is not a backup.
